prerequisites: fundamental learning outcomes for Probability and Random Variables
fundamental learning outcomes for Engineering Statistics

learning_outcomes.text: Defines forecasting problems and selects appropriate forecasting methods based on the type of data, the objective of the study, and error measures.
Computes confidence intervals, prediction intervals, and tolerance intervals, and quantitatively interprets uncertainty.
Applies hypothesis tests (one-sample and two-sample tests for proportions and means) and draws statistical inferences from test results.
Defines and applies time series forecasting models (moving average, exponential smoothing, AR, MA, ARMA, and ARIMA) and identifies the most appropriate model by comparing alternative models.
Constructs correlation and simple linear regression models, evaluates model assumptions, and analyzes forecasting uncertainties.
Constructs multiple linear regression models and evaluates issues related to variable selection, confounding, and multicollinearity.

syllabus_topics: Statistical Preliminaries and An Introduction to Forecasting A Review of Elementary Statistical Concepts
Forecasting and Data; Forecasting Methods; Errors in Forecasting
Choosing a Forecasting Technique Quantitative Forecasting Techniques
Some Case Studies on Bad Sampling
Confidence Intervals for Population Means (Large and Small Samples)
Confidence Intervals for Differences (Means and Proportions)
Hypothesis Tests for Population Means (Large and Small Samples)
Hypothesis Tests for Differences (Means and Proportions)
Time Series Forecasting Theory Types of Studies and Analysis; Cross-Sectional vs Time Series Data
Time Series Components and Processes; Model Selection
Moving Average, Weighted Moving Average, Exponential Smoothing
Forecasting Error; Examples in R Programming
AR, MA, ARMA, and ARIMA Models
The Least-Squares Line and Coefficient Uncertainty
